title: Word 9 — On the Incarnation of the Son of God
attribution_note: Word 9 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: The wonder of God made flesh

pairs.en: The very incarnation of the Son of God, His coming into the world, is itself a powerful spur to repentance for sinners. For whose sake did Christ come into the world? For sinners. To what end? For their salvation. Oh, how dearly God has valued our salvation! For our salvation, O sinners, He Himself came into the world. Listen, sinners, and understand! God Himself, for our salvation, came into the world — and came in our own form. O truly, *“great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh”* [1 Timothy 3:16]. *“Lord, what is man, that You are mindful of him?* *What is the son of man, that You care for him”* [Psalm 143:3]? Truly wondrous is God's goodness toward man, and wondrous is His incarnation! Foreseeing it, the prophet cried out to Him in fear and trembling: *“O Lord, I have heard the report of You, and was afraid.* *O Lord, I have considered Your works, and was amazed”* [Habakkuk 3:1–2].

sections.heading: What He bore for our sake

pairs.en: Sinners! Let us call to mind this great work of God, wrought for our sake, and let us repent. Let us remember how for our sake He was born of a Virgin, and was an infant, and was nourished at His mother's breast; how the Invisible became visible, the One without beginning took a beginning, and He who has no beginning was wrapped in swaddling clothes as a babe; how the Untouchable became touchable, and *“the Word became flesh”* [John 1:14]. Let us remember how, while still an infant, He fled from the murderous King Herod. Let us remember how He lived and wandered upon the earth, moving from place to place and laboring for our salvation; how He who is unapproachable even to the Cherubim and Seraphim dwelt among sinners; how He who has heaven for a throne and earth for a footstool, who dwells *“in unapproachable light,”* had *“nowhere to lay His head”* [1 Timothy 6:16; Matthew 8:20]; how *“though He was rich, yet for our sakes He became poor, that we through His poverty might become rich”* [2 Corinthians 8:9]. Let us remember how He who clothes Himself in light as with a garment wore instead a garment of corruptible cloth; how He who gives food to all flesh was fed on the bread of earth; how the All-Powerful became weak, and He who gives strength to all grew weary. Let us remember how lawless mouths blasphemed, reviled, and mocked Him who is above all honor and glory. Let us remember how He suffered, grieved, sorrowed, wept, and was filled with anguish. Let us remember how He was sold and betrayed by an ungrateful disciple, and abandoned by the rest of His disciples; how He was bound and led to judgment; how lawless men judged Him, struck Him, scourged Him, mocked Him, clothed Him in a robe of mockery, crowned Him with a crown of thorns, beat Him on the head with a reed, spat upon Him, and jeered at Him, saying, *“Hail, King of the Jews!”* [John 19:3]. Let us remember how He heard from His own lawless people: *“Away with Him, away with Him, crucify Him!”* [John 19:15] — how He was led to crucifixion with two criminals, and how the Son of God was crucified on the cross between two criminals, and died the death of the cross. All this the Son of God did for the sake of our salvation, O sinners!

sections.heading: The blood that cries out for repentance

pairs.en: In Adam we had lost salvation and all our blessedness, but Christ, the Son of God, by the good pleasure of His Heavenly Father, restored it to us. Let us judge for ourselves, sinners: does not the very Blood of Christ, shed for our salvation, and all His dispensation, cry out to us to repent, lest we be deprived of eternal salvation? For without repentance there is no salvation for anyone.

sections.heading: The peril of neglect, and the call to awaken

pairs.en: O poor sinner! Awaken and come to your senses. For if you do not, the very Blood of Christ, shed for you, will cry out against you for vengeance. Hear what the prophet of God says to you, in the person of God: *“I will reprove you, and set your sins in order before your eyes”* [Psalm 50:21]. That is, all your evil deeds, words, thoughts, designs, and undertakings will follow after you into that age and will appear at Christ's universal judgment, and you will receive for them your just recompense. If you will not now, to your own profit, repent, and so be saved by the grace of Christ, then you will repent later — but too late, and to no avail. *“Awake, you who sleep, and arise from the dead, and Christ will give you light”* [Ephesians 5:14], He who is *“God over all,”* blessed unto ages of ages. Amen.
